newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds end softer on Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds end softer on Greenspan comments.

text.p: 1600 GMT - Austrian bonds eased on Wednesday after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan voiced concern about inflation and said he could not rule out a pre-emptive tightening of monetary policy.
Traders said the market had drifted sidewards before the speech.
"We knew what he was going to talk about. It all depends on the emphasis," said one trader.
Greenspan also warned stock markets could overheat, but said the U.S. economy was basically in good condition.
The reaction of the cash market to Greenspan's comments remained subdued.
* 10 year benchmark 5.875 pct bond maturing July 2006 down 25 bps at 100.45 to yield 5.56 pct (5.53) in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 100.30/100.40 to yield 5.58/57.
* At the near end, five-year 5.50 percent bond maturing March 2001 down 20 bps at 104.25 to yield 4.39 percent in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 104.13/104.23 to yield 4.42/40 percent.
* AGB future down 43 bps at 109.99 on turnover of 286 lots.
* 10-year spread over Germany up one basis point at zero, five-year spread down seven at minus four.
* Money market rates stable with three-month VIBOR at 3.300 and overnight money just higher at 2.97/3.22.
